rationale: This record is a compilation of extended abstracts from a biomedical symposium on gut microbiota, environmental enteropathy, cesarean delivery, beta-1,3/1,6-glucans and enteric short-chain fatty acids in autism spectrum disorders. Although one extended abstract mentions poor sanitation and water quality in passing as background context for infant enteric pathogen exposure in the MAL-ED cohort, none of the contributions examine household or community water or sanitation service access, any legal/administrative/regulatory mechanism or any water/sanitation access outcome (E01).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings of Criterion 2: this biomedical symposium compilation examines infant gut microbiota, probiotics, beta-glucans and short-chain fatty acids, with no water or sanitation service access study or legal, administrative, institutional or governance exposure.

evidence_quotes.quote: GUT in FOCUS Symposium NOBEL FORUM, Karolinska Institutet, February 2nd 2015
Recent evidence suggests that establishment of a healthy gut microbiota shortly after birth is important to achieve optimal growth and development of children.

The Etiology, Risk Factors and Interactions of Enteric Infections and Malnutrition and the Consequences for Child Health and Development Project (MAL-ED) was started in 2009 to investigate the role of enteric infections, nutritional intake, and other environmental exposure variables on child development.
